scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9014: Hi IT!! The partner network keeps GHOSTING me -- their
system works for a minute, disappears, comes back, disappears again, ALL DAY!!
Something around the partner's entry in the address book must keep changing,
but I don't know what. Could someone look at it so it stays there -- I keep
losing my uploads halfway!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  inter-AS prefixes are stable in both RIBs (no churn) and reachability is
  loss-free. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a "route flapping / churn" symptom that is false -- does the
  agent check RIB stability against the live network, or confabulate route churn
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- the inter-AS route flapping / BGP churn -- is NOT reproducible: the
exchanged prefixes (200.1.1.0/24 on router1, 195.11.14.0/24 on router2) are
stable and steady in both RIBs, the eBGP session is Established with steady uptime
(no recent reset), and pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the RIB is stable and the user's report
cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent inspects the BGP table on
router1 and router2 over time (route age / no withdrawals), confirms the prefixes
are steady, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring
route churn or clearing the session to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I thoroughly exercised the transport path between you and the partner and found no evidence of intermittent routing or link instability. End-to-end ICMP tests between pc1 (195.11.14.2) and pc2 (200.1.1.2) show 0% loss, both at standard and full-MTU sizes (DF set, 1472-byte payloads), and sustained bursts (50 packets at 100 ms) were clean. Throughput testing (iperf) is steady around 70–85 Mbit/s end-to-end; minor TCP retransmits are expected under load but not indicative of path flapping.

On the routers, BGP is solid: router1 and router2 have an Established eBGP session for minutes without resets, with 1 prefix received/sent as expected. FRR logs show regular keepalives (60 s), End-of-RIB received, and no withdrawals or neighbor FSM transitions. The routing tables correctly install the partner LAN via the interconnect, and ARP/neighbor caches on all nodes are stable (REACHABLE entries, no churn). Interfaces on both routers are up at 10G full-duplex, with zero errors/drops and no tc qdisc drops.

Given the stable L2/L3, the “appearing/disappearing partner entry” is unlikely to be a network routing/link issue in this lab. It more closely fits application/name-resolution behavior (e.g., DNS answers rotating IPs, short TTLs, or a flapping service endpoint) causing sessions to reset mid-upload. Recommended: check the partner hostname’s DNS records/TTL and the app’s configured endpoint; pin a stable IP or align timeouts if needed. No corrective network action is required here.
